text:
Brandon Hagel is back from injured reserve, and the Lightning have lost both games since. Don't blame him for that, though the numbers have been unkind to him all season.

Hagel has 13 goals on 12.96 expected goals, so his own finishing is exactly on schedule. The problem is everyone else: with him on the ice, Tampa has scored 9.1 fewer goals than its chances deserved, one of the biggest gaps in the league. Those chances are excellent. The Lightning get 63% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had him 99th percentile among forwards for driving play last season. That kind of bad luck usually swings back, and when it does, his assists come with it.

He's a sixth-round pick who turned into a two-way first-liner, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why: 97th percentile among forwards for setting up shots, and plenty of looks off passes across the slot. Watch his ice time first. He's averaging 19 minutes over his last ten, two and a half less than before the injury. Our range puts him between 70 and 95 points.
